results.title: MCP Integration for agents
excerpts:
* Login

MCP Integration for agents

LiveAgent exposes a built-in MCP server (Model Context Protocol) that lets you connect external AI tools, such as ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, Cursor, claude.ai, FlowHunt , or any other MCP-compatible client, directly with your LiveAgent account. Once connected, your own AI tools/agents can read ticket data and perform actions on your behalf, using your agent identity and permissions.
There are two ways to authenticate your MCP client - OAuth 2.1 (recommended) , where the AI tool discovers the authorization server automatically and redirects you to a consent screen, or Bearer token , where you generate an MCP access token in your profile and paste it into the AI tool's configuration manually.

In this article

* Finding MCP Integration in your profile
* Connecting with OAuth
* How it works
* Managing authorized apps
* Connecting with a bearer token
* Generating an access token
* Managing access tokens
* Permissions and vailable tools

Finding MCP Integration in your profile

1. Click your avatar in the top-right corner of the LiveAgent panel and select Edit profile .
2. In the left-hand menu, navigate to the MCP Integration section.
This screen shows your connection details and access tokens. Use these values to configure any MCP-compatible client:
* Setting | Value
* MCP server URL | /api/mcp
* Transport protocol | Streamable HTTP
* Authentication | OAuth 2.1 (Authorization Code + PKCE) or Bearer token

Connecting with OAuth

OAuth authentication lets AI tools connect to your LiveAgent MCP server without you having to generate, copy, and paste a token. The tool handles the entire authentication flow automatically using standard OAuth 2.1 with PKCE.

How it works

1. In your AI tool (for example Claude app), add a new MCP server/connector/plugin using your LiveAgent MCP server URL.
2. The AI tool calls that URL, receives a discovery hint, and fetches LiveAgent's OAuth server metadata automatically.
3. You are redirected to the LiveAgent login page (if not already logged in) and then to a consent screen asking you to approve the connection.
4. After you approve, the tool receives an access token and is ready to use.
Note: Your consent decision is remembered. If you remove and reconnect the same tool later, the consent screen is skipped and completes silently.

Managing authorized apps

The MCP Integration screen in your profile lists all OAuth clients you have approved under Authorized apps . You can revoke any authorized app. The tool will lose access immediately and will need to go through the OAuth flow again to reconnect.
Tip: Administrators or users with a custom role with the permission to manage agents can view and revoke authorized apps for other agents in the account.

Connecting with a bearer token

If your AI tool does not support OAuth authentication, you can use a bearer token to connect it. Bearer tokens are MCP access tokens you generate in your profile and paste directly into your MCP client. Bearer tokens are also used by scripts that require manual configuration.

Generating an access token

1. On the MCP Integration screen in your profile and click Generate token .
2. Copy the access token.
3. Paste the access token into your MCP client as the Bearer token value.
Important: Store the access token securely as soon as you generate it. If you lose it, you will need to revoke the existing token and generate a new one.
You can generate up to 10 active access tokens per account. Having multiple tokens is useful if you connect the same account to more than one tool or device.

Managing access tokens

The access token list on the MCP Integration screen shows each token's masked identifier and expiration date. Each can be revoked independently without affecting the others. Upon revoking a token, the corresponding MCP client/AI tool will lose access immediately.
Note: Access tokens expire automatically after two years from the date they were generated, regardless of how frequently they are used. Plan to rotate access tokens before they expire to avoid interruption.

Permissions and available tools

Regardless of whether you connect via OAuth or bearer token, your AI tool has access to the full set of LiveAgent MCP tools. See the MCP tools reference for the complete list of tools and their detailed description.
All actions are performed under your agent identity and are subject to your role's permissions, exactly as if you had performed them in the LiveAgent panel.

results.title: MCP Integration for Agents
excerpts:
MCP Integration for Agents

LiveAgent exposes a built-in MCP server (Model Context Protocol) that lets you connect external AI tools — such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, claude.ai, FlowHunt , or any other MCP-compatible client — directly to your LiveAgent account. Once connected, those tools can read ticket data and perform actions on your behalf, using your agent identity and permissions.
Note: Your AI agents use LiveAgent's built-in MCP tools. Connecting external MCP servers inside LiveAgent is not supported yet.
There are two ways to authenticate your MCP client:
* Bearer token — generate an MCP access token in your profile and paste it into the client manually.
* OAuth 2.1 — the client discovers the authorization server automatically and redirects you to a consent screen. No manual token handling required.

Finding MCP Integration in Your Profile

1. Click your avatar in the top-right corner of the LiveAgent panel and select Edit profile .
2. In the left-hand menu, select MCP Integration .
This screen shows your connection details, access tokens, and authorized OAuth apps. Use these values when configuring any MCP-compatible client:
* Setting | Value
* MCP server URL | https://<your-liveagent-domain>/api/mcp
* Transport protocol | Streamable HTTP
* Authentication | Bearer token or OAuth 2.1 (Authorization Code + PKCE)

Connecting with a Bearer Token

Bearer tokens are MCP access tokens you generate in your profile and paste directly into your MCP client. Best for desktop tools and scripts that require manual configuration.

Generating an access token

1. On the MCP Integration screen, click Generate token .
2. Copy the access token immediately — it is displayed only once and cannot be retrieved later.
3. Paste the access token into your MCP client as the Bearer token value.
Important: Store the access token securely as soon as you generate it. If you lose it, you will need to revoke the existing token and generate a new one.
You can generate up to 10 active access tokens per account. Having multiple tokens is useful if you connect the same account to more than one tool or device — each can be revoked independently without affecting the others.
Note: Access tokens expire automatically after two years from the date they were generated, regardless of how frequently they are used. Plan to rotate access tokens before they expire to avoid interruption.

Managing access tokens

The access token list on the MCP Integration screen shows each token's masked identifier and expiration date. You can revoke any individual access token — the corresponding MCP client will lose access immediately.

Connecting with OAuth

OAuth lets AI tools connect to your LiveAgent MCP server without you having to copy and paste a token. The tool handles the entire authentication flow automatically using standard OAuth 2.1 with PKCE.

How it works

1. In the AI tool (for example claude.ai), add your LiveAgent MCP server URL: https://<your-liveagent-domain>/api/mcp
2. The tool contacts that URL, receives a discovery hint, and fetches LiveAgent's OAuth server metadata automatically.
3. You are redirected to the LiveAgent login page (if not already logged in) and then to a consent screen asking you to approve the connection.
4. After you approve, the tool receives an access token and is ready to use. No manual copy-paste required.
Note: Your consent decision is remembered. If you connect the same tool again later, the consent screen is skipped and the flow completes silently.

Managing authorized apps

The MCP Integration screen in your profile lists all OAuth clients you have approved under Authorized apps . You can revoke any authorized app — the tool will lose access immediately and will need to go through the OAuth flow again to reconnect.
Administrators with the agent management privilege can view and revoke authorized apps for any agent in the account.

Available Tools

Regardless of whether you connect via Bearer token or OAuth, your AI tool has access to the full set of LiveAgent MCP tools. All actions are performed under your agent identity and are subject to your role's permissions. See the MCP Tools Reference for the complete list of tools and what each one does.
Note: Unlike AI agents — which run automatically via rules on your chosen AI provider and restrict the tool set per agent configuration — personal MCP access tokens give access to all tools. Your role's permissions still apply — actions your role is not permitted to perform will be rejected.

results.title: API key
excerpts:
# API key


## What is an API key

API key is an identity of your LiveAgent (like your username and password) which you can use to build your own custom integration solutions. Never give it to anybody you don't trust. If your API key is lost, do not hesitate to generate a new one! Anybody with your API key can fully access your LiveAgent.

## How can I get my API key

While logged in as an admin navigate to Configuration> System> API which loads the API v3 section where you find existing API keys or add a new one. To access the API v1 section click the Settings for API v1 link under the API v3 header.

This is how the API v1 section looks where you have settings for your API v1 key.

When adding a new API key in v3 you have an option to define permissions for this key (as you can have more keys you can also give **different keys to different people with different permissions** ).

## Can I change the API key?

Yes both API versions have options to generate new keys and invalidate existing ones.

**IMPORTANT NOTE:** Do not forget that when you generate a new API key for your LiveAgent ALL clients using the old key will stop working immediately !

## API v3 use

Your API key has to be set in header of your requests:

curl --location --request GET 'your.ladesk.com/api/v3/tickets' \\  
\--header 'apikey: 0865evv883j6auflvlt7zrwgqn32qo74' \\  
\--header 'Content-Type: application/json'

Here's an example of cURL code in PHP:

```
curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, array('Accept: application/json', ' **apikey: 123456_YOUR_API_KEY_123456** '));
```

Updated: Mar 16, 2021

Let Claude Desktop and other MCP-compatible AI clients search, tag, and act on your tickets directly — inside the same permissions your agents already have.

Model Context Protocol

A standard way for AI tools to plug into your help desk

MCP is an open standard for connecting AI applications to outside tools and data. LiveAgent's MCP server exposes tickets, ticket messages , knowledge base articles, agents, and departments as tools an MCP-compatible AI client can call directly — no custom integration required.
* Search and read tickets, messages, and knowledge base articles
* Tag, assign, transfer, resolve, and reopen tickets
* List agents and departments to route work correctly
* Reply to WhatsApp conversations where enabled
See LiveAgent's REST API

MCP server

Built for teams already using an AI client

If your team already relies on Claude Desktop or another MCP-compatible AI client day-to-day, connect it once and let it work with live ticket data instead of a static export.
What your AI client can help with:
* Triage and tag incoming tickets
* Summarize long ticket threads on request
* Look up knowledge base answers while chatting with you
* Route tickets to the right department

Access stays inside your existing permissions

Connecting an AI client isn't a one-click, all-access step. It runs through an OAuth 2.1 authorization flow with a consent screen, so you approve exactly which account it acts as.
What stays under your control:
* Every ticket action is checked against that account's department and role permissions
* Access tokens are scoped to approved actions, not blanket account access
* Individual tools, like WhatsApp replies, can be turned off

How It works?

Click Generate token

Click Generate token.

Copy it right away

Paste it into your AI tool

Every tool your AI client can call

LiveAgent’s MCP server gives a connected AI client 33 tools to work with, covering tickets, custom fields, the knowledge base, and more. Every tool still respects the connecting account’s own department and role permissions, so an AI client never sees or does more than the agent it’s acting as.

Tickets

* What it does for you | Tool
* Finds tickets matching a keyword, status, or other filter, so your AI client can pull up the right one without you searching manually | search_tickets
* Reads a ticket’s full conversation, message by message, so it has real context before doing anything | get_ticket_messages
* Checks a ticket’s details — status, channel, and other metadata | get_ticket_metadata
* Sees what tags exist on the account | get_tags

...

LiveAgent's MCP server lets you connect an MCP-compatible AI client, like Claude Desktop, directly to your LiveAgent account. Once connected, the AI client can search tickets, read conversations, add tags, and take other actions you've approved, without an agent copying data between apps.
What can a connected AI tool do in LiveAgent? A connected AI tool can search and read tickets, view ticket messages and knowledge base articles, tag, assign, transfer, resolve, and reopen tickets, list agents and departments, and reply to WhatsApp conversations where that channel is enabled. Every action still respects the permissions of the account it connects as.
How is access secured? Connecting an AI client requires an authorization flow (OAuth 2.1 with PKCE) and a consent screen, so you explicitly approve which account the AI client can act as. Access tokens are scoped, and every ticket-level action is checked against that account's own department and role permissions before it runs.
Which AI clients work with LiveAgent's MCP server? Any AI client that supports the Model Context Protocol can connect, including Claude Desktop. As MCP adoption grows across other AI tools, the same connection works with them too, since it's built on the open MCP standard rather than a single vendor's client.

excerpts:
MCP Tools Reference

This article lists all tools exposed by the LiveAgent MCP server. The same tool set is available in both contexts:
* Personal MCP connections (Bearer token or OAuth 2.1) — all tools are available automatically, subject to your role's permissions.
* AI agent MCP connections — the administrator selects an allowed-tools subset when configuring the agent; tools not in that list are blocked even if the flow requests them.
For setup instructions, see MCP Integration for Agents (personal connections) or AI Agents feature overview (automated agents).

In this article

* Read tools
* Write tools
* Knowledge base tools

Read tools

* Tool | What it does
* Get ticket messages | Retrieve ticket messages; omit the cursor for a full initial fetch, or provide a cursor to fetch only messages newer than a previous response
* Get ticket metadata | Read ticket properties such as subject, timestamps, status, priority, department, and assigned agent
* Get tags | Read the tags currently applied to the ticket
* Get ticket notes | Retrieve internal ticket notes (agent notes, rule notes, API notes) with cursor-based pagination

# MCP Integration for agents

LiveAgent exposes a built-in **MCP server** (Model Context Protocol) that lets you connect external AI tools, such as ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, Cursor, claude.ai, FlowHunt, or any other MCP-compatible client, directly with your LiveAgent account. Once connected, your own AI tools/agents can read ticket data and perform actions on your behalf, using your agent identity and permissions.

There are two ways to authenticate your MCP client - **OAuth 2.1 (recommended)**, where the AI tool discovers the authorization server automatically and redirects you to a consent screen, or **Bearer token**, where you generate an MCP access token in your profile and paste it into the AI tool's configuration manually.

## Finding MCP Integration in your profile

1. Click your avatar in the top-right corner of the LiveAgent panel and select **Edit profile**.
2. In the left-hand menu, navigate to the **MCP Integration** section.

This screen shows your connection details and access tokens. Use these values to configure any MCP-compatible client:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **MCP server URL** | https://<your-liveagent-domain>/api/mcp |
| **Transport protocol** | Streamable HTTP |
| **Authentication** | OAuth 2.1 (Authorization Code + PKCE) or Bearer token |

## Connecting with OAuth

OAuth authentication lets AI tools connect to your LiveAgent MCP server without you having to generate, copy, and paste a token. The tool handles the entire authentication flow automatically using standard OAuth 2.1 with PKCE.

### How it works

1. In your AI tool (for example Claude app), add a new MCP server/connector/plugin using your LiveAgent MCP server URL.
2. The AI tool calls that URL, receives a discovery hint, and fetches LiveAgent's OAuth server metadata automatically.
3. You are redirected to the LiveAgent login page (if not already logged in) and then to a **consent screen** asking you to approve the connection.
4. After you approve, the tool receives an access token and is ready to use.

**Note:** Your consent decision is remembered. If you remove and reconnect the same tool later, the consent screen is skipped and completes silently.

### Managing authorized apps

The **MCP Integration** screen in your profile lists all OAuth clients you have approved under **Authorized apps**. You can revoke any authorized app. The tool will lose access immediately and will need to go through the OAuth flow again to reconnect.

Tip: Administrators or users with a custom role with the permission to manage agents can view and revoke authorized apps for other agents in the account.

## Connecting with a bearer token

If your AI tool does not support OAuth authentication, you can use a bearer token to connect it. Bearer tokens are MCP access tokens you generate in your profile and paste directly into your MCP client. Bearer tokens are also used by scripts that require manual configuration.

### Generating an access token

1. On the **MCP Integration** screen in your profile and click **Generate token**.
2. Copy the access token.
3. Paste the access token into your MCP client as the Bearer token value.

**Important:** Store the access token securely as soon as you generate it. If you lose it, you will need to revoke the existing token and generate a new one.

You can generate up to **10 active access tokens** per account. Having multiple tokens is useful if you connect the same account to more than one tool or device.

### Managing access tokens

The access token list on the MCP Integration screen shows each token's masked identifier and expiration date. Each can be revoked independently without affecting the others. Upon revoking a token, the corresponding MCP client/AI tool will lose access immediately.

**Note:** Access tokens expire automatically after **two years** from the date they were generated, regardless of how frequently they are used. Plan to rotate access tokens before they expire to avoid interruption.

# Connect AI tools to LiveAgent with MCP

Let ChatGPT, Claude and other MCP-compatible AI clients search, tag, and act on your tickets directly — inside the same permissions your agents already have.

No setup fee
24/7 Customer service
No credit card required
Cancel any time
30-day free trial

Model Context Protocol

## A standard way for AI tools to plug into your help desk

MCP is an open standard for connecting AI applications to outside tools and data. LiveAgent's MCP server exposes tickets, ticket messages, knowledge base articles, agents, and departments as tools an MCP-compatible AI client can call directly — no custom integration required.

* Search and read tickets, messages, and knowledge base articles
* Tag, assign, transfer, resolve, and reopen tickets
* List agents and departments to route work correctly
* Reply to WhatsApp conversations where enabled

* Triage and tag incoming tickets
* Summarize long ticket threads on request
* Look up knowledge base answers while chatting with you
* Route tickets to the right department

Connecting an AI client isn't an all-access step. It uses an access token you generate in your own profile, or an OAuth 2.1 sign-in with a consent screen, so it always acts as one account you approved.
